User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the BillBully application.

plaidAccessToken.description: Plaid access token for connecting to bank accounts.

creditReportConsent.description: Indicates if the user has given consent to pull credit reports.

Bill.title: Bill
Bill.description: Represents a bill for a user.

companyName.description: Name of the company the bill is from.

category.description: Category of the bill (cable, phone, insurance).

status.description: Status of the bill (pending, negotiating, success, failed).

savingsAmount.description: Amount saved on the bill through negotiation.

CreditItem.title: CreditItem
CreditItem.description: Represents an item on a user's credit report.

id.description: Unique identifier for the credit item.

bureau.description: Credit bureau the item is from (equifax, transunion, experian).

accountName.description: Name of the account the item is related to.

accountNumber.description: Account number of the account the item is related to.

type.description: Type of credit item (late_payment, collection, charge_off).

status.description: Status of the credit item (identified, disputed, deleted, verified).

responseDeadline.description: Deadline for the credit bureau to respond.

DisputeLetter.title: DisputeLetter
DisputeLetter.description: Represents a dispute letter sent for a credit item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the dispute letter.

trackingNumber.description: Tracking number for the mailed letter.

responseReceived.description: Indicates if a response has been received.

billingFrequency.description: How often the subscription is billed.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to ensure authorization independence, support secure list operations (QAPs), and maintain data clarity. It uses path-based ownership for user-specific data and denormalization where necessary to avoid `get()` calls in security rules.

**Authorization Independence:** User-owned data is stored under `/users/{userId}`, granting the user implicit ownership. The Bills, CreditItems, DisputesLetters, and Subscriptions entities are stored as subcollections of the user document, ensuring clear ownership and authorization independence. Access control relies on `request.auth.uid` matching the `userId` in the path, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to parent documents.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):** The structure facilitates secure `list` operations by segregating data based on ownership. Listing bills, credit items, dispute letters, and subscriptions is restricted to the owning user via path-based rules. This avoids the need to filter based on user ID within the rules, improving security and performance.

**Data Clarity and Predictability:**  Explicit state modeling is encouraged with the `status` field in the Bill and CreditItem entities. Semantic naming conventions are used throughout the structure.
